summary: KIRI Engine is a phone and web scanner from KIRI Innovation with a free tier, and it is the most open of the consumer capture products: alongside the closed application sits a set of separately licensed open-source pieces — a Blender add-on for importing, editing, animating and exporting splats, an After Effects plug-in, a desktop tool for preparing images and 360 footage, and, most interesting to a standards audience, colmap4d, a frozen version 1.0 specification with a conformance suite that adds a timestamp to every image and every point of a COLMAP model. It captures four ways — photogrammetry, lidar, a neural method for shiny and featureless objects, and Gaussian splatting — and it exports more than anything else in this lane: OBJ, STL, FBX, glTF, GLB, USDZ, PLY and XYZ. Two things make it matter here. Its splat captures come with a mesh, and that mesh then reaches the product's mesh features, including automatic skeleton generation, which is the only path in this whole map from a phone capture of a real thing to something with bones in it. And its open-source work is where the time problem is being attacked in the open, by a specification with golden test fixtures rather than by a private file variant. What it does not do is carry rights, authorship or any statement of scale in what it writes, and its splat editing and rigging live inside the service rather than in any format a second implementation could read.

coverage.note: Splats and meshes are drawn in the application, in a browser preview and, through the open add-on, inside Blender's own renderer. None of the product's own pipeline is described; the add-on's is Blender's.
